checks.prototypes_vs_gcc: Probed GAP9 GCC 7.1.1 and this clang with the same bad-argument file. GCC's diagnostics give expected 'void *','int' for fenced and 'void *','void *','int' for OffsetedWritePtr, and clang reports the same parameter types. const/volatile pointer arguments: GCC -Wdiscarded-qualifiers warning, clang -Wincompatible-pointer-types-discards-qualifiers warning. Integer as pointer: GCC warning, clang error (-Wint-conversion, clang 16+ default, same as every other builtin). Too few arguments is an error in both. Using OffsetedWritePtr's void result is an error in both. _Generic on the fenced result gives int in both (static assert passes). The PMSIS shapes (void*)base, (int*)base, (int*)value compile in C and C++ with no diagnostic. Without xpulpv, clang says 'needs target feature xpulpv'.
checks.fenced_semantics: IR: declare i32 @llvm.riscv.pulp.event.unit.read.fenced(ptr, i32) #{nounwind}, which means any memory effect, not willreturn, side effects. MIR: PULP_ELW is hasSideEffects=1, mayStore=1. At -O2, -O3 and -Os, clang keeps 2 p.elw for two calls, 2 p.elw zero for two unused calls, 16 p.elw for a fully unrolled 16-iteration loop, and the p.elw inside the hardware-loop body for used and unused results. It reloads a pointer or global load across p.elw (no CSE), keeps a store that is overwritten after p.elw (no DSE), does not hoist the invariant load out of the loop past p.elw, keeps store/p.elw order in the loop, and keeps the order volatile store, p.elw, volatile store, volatile load. The only thing it optimises across p.elw is a non-escaped local array, which no call can reach. That is legal and GCC does the same. Unused result gives p.elw zero where GCC uses a scratch register. I accept this: RISCVDeadRegisterDefinitions deliberately also rewrites side-effecting loads, a load to x0 still performs the access per the RISC-V spec, GVSoC Lsu::elw still issues data_req with x0 mapped to null_reg (regfile_implem.hpp:29-32), and the existing event_unit_read already behaves this way. The note states it.
checks.offsetedwriteptr_semantics: IR: declare void @llvm.riscv.pulp.OffsetedWritePtr(ptr, ptr nocapture writeonly, i32) #{nounwind memory(write)}, not willreturn and not argmemonly. So DSE cannot remove it: isRemovable needs willreturn and getForDest needs argmemonly. The result of one call is never reused for another, and since it may write any memory, a later load is not forwarded across it. Machine level: the selected SW/P_SW_rr has no memoperand (checked with -stop-after=finalize-isel), so it counts as an ordered memory reference and is never dead. Checked at -O2, -O3 and -Os. A store to a dead local array (with &g as value, and twice with the same value) is kept. Two stores to the same address stay two. A load after it is re-read. A later plain store to the same address does not remove it, and a plain store before it is kept too. A local read-after gives sw zero; sw v; lw (re-read). Stores in loops (n, 16-unrolled, do-while) stay one per iteration, with no LICM hoist. GCC output is the same, including GCC's 'Offseted Write volatile' stores to dead local arrays. The worker's TableGen explanation for not using IntrHasSideEffects is consistent with SW/P_SW_rr being hasSideEffects=0, and the argument holds without it.
checks.addressing_vs_gcc: OffsetedWritePtr: offsets 2047 and -2048 give sw imm(rs1) in both (GCC prints p.sw imm, which is the same instruction). Offsets 2048, -2049 and 4100 give a materialised register plus p.sw rs2,rs3(rs1) in both (clang lui/addi or li/slli, GCC li/add). A register offset gives p.sw rs2,rs3(rs1) in both. Fenced: 2047 and -2048 give p.elw imm(rs1). 2048 and -2049 give add + p.elw 0 in clang, while GCC emits p.elw 2048(a0) / -2049(a0), which its own assembler rejects ('illegal operands'), so clang is right there. A register offset gives add + p.elw 0 in clang; GCC rejects a non-constant offset. The worker reported both GCC points under other_errors_seen.
